raw_text:
Great — below is a 12-week progressive hypertrophy program tailored for a 26‑year‑old female recreational lifter who follows a strict vegan diet and wants to gain muscle. It includes phase progression, week-by-week training split, detailed session plans (exercises, sets, reps, tempo, rest), and a practical vegan nutrition plan designed to hit ~150 g protein/day plus recovery guidance and sample meals/snacks, supplement suggestions, and monitoring tips.

Assumptions and goals
- Goal: muscle gain (hypertrophy) across 12 weeks.
- Training status: recreational lifter (familiar with main lifts and gym equipment).
- Equipment: full gym available (barbells, dumbbells, cable machines, squat rack, leg press, pulleys, machines, benches).
- Nutrition target: ~150 g protein/day from plant sources only.
- Calorie guidance: modest surplus (~+250–500 kcal/day above maintenance; adjust per progress/body-composition goals).
- Progressive overload across phases with deloads every 4th week built into plan.
- Emphasis on compound lifts, adequate volume, balanced push/pull/legs split, accessory work for symmetry.

Program structure (overview)
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (Upper/Lower ×2) — balance of volume and recovery for hypertrophy.
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–4 (Foundation / Volume): build work capacity, technique, moderate intensity (65–75% 1RM relative effort).
  - Weeks 5–8 (Intensity / Hypertrophy Emphasis): increase load and density, more heavy sets (70–85% RPE), more emphasis on progressive overload.
  - Weeks 9–12 (Peak Volume with Strength Focus + Taper): highest intensity for compound lifts then slight taper in final week for recovery and assessment.
- Deloads: Week 4 and Week 8 are planned as lighter recovery weeks (reduced volume/intensity ~40–60%).
- Rep ranges: mostly 6–15 reps suited to hypertrophy; some lower-rep strength sets for compound lifts in later phases.

Progression key
- Weeks 1–3: add small load or 1–2 reps per set each week where possible.
- Week 4: deload at 50–60% volume/intensity.
- Weeks 5–7: increase working loads ~5–10% on main lifts versus Week 3, keep accessory volume similar or slightly increased.
- Week 8: deload (same approach as Week 4).
- Weeks 9–11: push for new personal bests on main compounds and finish with higher volume accessory work.
- Week 12: taper volume slightly, maintain intensity for singles/doubles or end with moderate hypertrophy work to consolidate gains.

Weekly layout (applies to most weeks)
- Day 1: Upper A (Horizontal push/pull focus + arms, core)
- Day 2: Lower A (Squat/glute bias + hamstrings)
- Day 3: Rest or active recovery (light mobility, walking)
- Day 4: Upper B (Vertical push/pull focus + chest emphasis)
- Day 5: Lower B (Deadlift/hinge bias + quads)
- Day 6–7: Rest/recovery; optionally light cardio or mobility

Detailed 12‑week plan

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4 (Foundation / Volume)
General cues: focus on clean technique, full ROM, 2–3 warmup sets before heavy compound sets. Tempo: control eccentric (2s), pause 0–1s, explosive concentric. Rest: 60–120s for compounds, 45–75s for accessories.

Week 1
Day 1 — Upper A
1. Barbell bench press — 4×8 (RPE ~7)  
2. Bent-over barbell row or chest-supported row — 4×8  
3. Incline dumbbell press — 3×10  
4. Seated cable row (neutral) — 3×10  
5. Dumbbell lateral raise — 3×12–15  
6. EZ-bar or cable curl — 3×10  
7. Rope pressdown — 3×12  
8. Plank — 3×45–60s

Day 2 — Lower A
1. Back squat — 4×8  
2. Romanian deadlift (RDL) — 3×8–10  
3. Leg press — 3×12  
4. Bulgarian split squat — 3×10 each leg  
5. Lying leg curl or seated hamstring curl — 3×12  
6. Standing calf raise — 4×12–15  
7. Hanging knee raises — 3×12

Day 4 — Upper B
1. Overhead press (barbell or dumbbell) — 4×8  
2. Pull-up (assisted or weighted) or lat pulldown — 4×8–10  
3. Dumbbell bench press (flat) — 3×10  
4. Single-arm dumbbell row — 3×10 each side  
5. Face pulls — 3×15  
6. Hammer curl — 3×12  
7. Triceps overhead extension (rope or dumbbell) — 3×12

Day 5 — Lower B
1. Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) — 4×6–8  
2. Front squat or goblet squat — 3×8–10  
3. Hip thrust — 4×10  
4. Reverse lunges — 3×10 each leg  
5. Cable pull-through or glute-ham raise — 3×12  
6. Seated calf raise — 4×12–15  
7. Side plank — 3×30–45s each side

Weeks 2–3
- Keep same exercise selection. Increase load slightly (2.5–5 kg on upper lifts if form is perfect) or add 1–2 reps per set. Maintain RPE 7–8 on top sets.
- Optionally swap accessory variations (e.g., incline bench to close-grip incline; RDL to single-leg RDL) to add variety.

Week 4 — Deload
- Reduce sets by ~40–50% or use 50–60% of the previous working weights and keep technique focus.
- Example: Compounds 3×5 at 50–60% of usual load, accessories 2×10 lighter.
- Keep movement but reduce fatigue accumulation.

PHASE 2 — Weeks 5–8 (Hypertrophy + Increasing Intensity)
Goal: increase working intensities, add some heavier sets and denser sessions. Small increase in accessory volume.

Week 5
Day 1 — Upper A
1. Barbell bench press — 5×6 (slightly heavier; RPE 8)  
2. Pendlay or chest-supported row — 4×6–8  
3. Incline dumbbell press — 3×8–10  
4. Weighted pull-up or heavy lat pulldown — 4×8  
5. Dumbbell lateral raise superset with front raise — 3×12/12  
6. Preacher or incline curls — 3×10  
7. Triceps cable pressdown — 3×10–12  
8. Pallof press — 3×12 each side

Day 2 — Lower A
1. Back squat — 5×6  
2. Romanian deadlift — 4×8  
3. Leg press — 4×10 (heavier)  
4. Bulgarian split squat — 3×8 each leg (add dumbbells)  
5. Hamstring curl (machine) — 4×10  
6. Calf raise — 4×12–15  
7. Ab wheel or cable crunch — 3×12–15

Day 4 — Upper B
1. Strict overhead press — 5×6  
2. Barbell or dumbbell row — 4×8  
3. Flat dumbbell press — 3×8–10 (heavier)  
4. Chest-supported incline row or single-arm cable row — 3×10  
5. Face pulls — 4×15  
6. Alternating curls — 3×10  
7. Skull crushers (EZ or rope) — 3×10

Day 5 — Lower B
1. Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) — 5×5 (focus on strength)  
2. Front squat — 4×6–8  
3. Hip thrust — 4×8–10 (heavier)  
4. Walking lunges — 3×12 each leg  
5. Cable pull-through — 3×12  
6. Calf raise — 4×12–15  
7. Plank variations — 3×60s

Week 6–7
- Add weight to main lifts if form maintained. For accessories, aim to increase time under tension, add slow eccentrics or a top set to failure on one accessory per session.
- Small weekly increases (2–5% load) on compounds if last session was manageable.

Week 8 — Deload
- Same deload protocol as week 4: reduce volume/intensity ~40–60%. Keep technique and mobility.

PHASE 3 — Weeks 9–12 (Peak Volume + Strength Emphasis)
Goal: push for heavier single/double top sets on compounds in Weeks 9–11, then drop volume and keep moderate intensity for Week 12 for consolidation and recovery.

Week 9
Day 1 — Upper A (slightly heavier)
1. Bench press — 4×5 heavy (RPE 8–9)  
2. Barbell row — 4×6  
3. Incline DB press — 3×8  
4. Weighted pull-ups or heavy lat pulldown — 3×6–8  
5. Lateral raise dropset — 3 sets (12 then drop weight to failure)  
6. Barbell curls — 3×8  
7. Cable triceps extension — 3×10  
8. Cable anti-rotation hold — 3×10 each side

Day 2 — Lower A
1. Squat — 4×5 heavy  
2. RDL — 4×6–8  
3. Bulgarian split squat or single-leg press — 3×8 each leg  
4. Hip thrust — 4×6–8 (heavy)  
5. Hamstring curl — 3×10  
6. Calves — 4×10–12  
7. Hanging leg raises — 3×12

Day 4 — Upper B
1. Overhead press — 4×5 heavy  
2. Bent-over row — 4×6  
3. Flat DB press (heavy) — 3×6–8  
4. Single-arm cable row — 3×8  
5. Face pulls — 3×20 (higher rep focus)  
6. Hammer curls — 3×10  
7. Dips (assisted or weighted) or close-grip bench — 3×8–10

Day 5 — Lower B
1. Deadlift — 4×4 heavy (work up to heavy set)  
2. Front squat — 3×6–8  
3. Hip thrust (pause at top) — 4×6–8  
4. Reverse lunges — 3×10 each leg  
5. Good mornings or back extensions — 3×10–12  
6. Calves — 4×12  
7. Plank with variations — 3 rounds

Week 10–11
- Continue to push for progressive overload in main lifts. Week 11 can include a planned attempt at 1–3 rep PRs for compound lifts if safe and desired — but keep warm-up sets and reduce accessory work that day to conserve energy.
- Accessories remain focused on hypertrophy and weak point training.

Week 12 — Taper/Consolidation
- Reduce weekly volume ~20–30% but keep one or two moderately heavy sets (RPE 7–8) on main lifts to maintain strength signals.
- Do not attempt maximal PRs; focus on form, recovery and nutrition.
- Example: Compounds 3×4–6 at 85% of prior heavy weight; accessories 2×10 lighter.

Exercise substitution examples
- If shoulder pain: substitute barbell OHP with seated DB press, reduce range, increase face pulls and external rotation work.
- If limited on heavy deadlifts: use trap-bar deadlift or deficit/blocks variations.
- Swap machine for free weights and vice versa to manage fatigue.

Nutrition plan — hitting ~150 g protein/day (vegan)
Guidelines
- Aim for a calorie surplus of +250–500 kcal/day above estimated maintenance. Starting point: estimate maintenance via 14–16 kcal/kg bodyweight depending on activity, then add surplus. Monitor weight gain ~0.25–0.5 kg/week and adjust.
- Protein: 150 g/day (~1.6–2.0 g/kg for many lifters depending on bodyweight; adjust to client's weight if needed).
- Distribute protein across 3–5 meals; aim for ~25–40 g protein per meal and protein-containing snack(s).
- Include leucine-rich sources (soy, pea, wheat, lentils, chickpeas) and varied plant proteins for amino acid completeness.
- Prioritize whole foods, fortified foods (B12, vitamin D), and consider protein powders for convenience.

Protein sources and approximate protein per typical serving
- Soy products: tofu (100 g ≈ 8–12 g), tempeh (100 g ≈ 19 g), edamame (1 cup ≈ 17 g)  
- Seitan (vital wheat gluten): 100 g ≈ 25 g (very protein-dense)  
- Legumes: lentils (1 cup cooked ≈ 18 g), chickpeas (1 cup ≈ 15 g), black beans (1 cup ≈ 15 g)  
- Protein powders: pea protein isolate, soy protein isolate, blend (20–30 g protein per scoop)  
- Soy milk/fortified plant milk: 1 cup ≈ 6–8 g (soy milk higher)  
- Nuts/seeds: peanut butter (2 tbsp ≈ 8 g), hemp seeds (3 tbsp ≈ 10 g), chia seeds (2 tbsp ≈ 4 g)  
- Whole grains: quinoa (1 cup cooked ≈ 8 g), oats (1 cup cooked ≈ 6 g)  

Sample daily meal plan to reach ~150 g protein
(Adjust portion sizes to meet calorie surplus)

Option A — High-protein day (~150 g)
- Breakfast:
  - Tofu scramble (200 g tofu ≈ 20–24 g protein) with veggies + 1 cup cooked oats (6 g) made with 1 cup soy milk (8 g)  
  - Totals: ~34–38 g

- Mid-morning snack:
  - Smoothie with 1.5 scoops pea/soy protein powder (1 scoop ≈ 24 g — so 36 g), 1 tbsp peanut butter (8 g), frozen fruit, water or soy milk  
  - Totals: ~44 g (cumulative ~78 g)

- Lunch:
  - Tempeh salad/bowl: 150 g tempeh (≈28 g) + quinoa 1 cup cooked (8 g) + veggies + tahini dressing (2 tbsp tahini ≈ 6 g)  
  - Totals: ~42 g (cum ~120 g)

- Afternoon snack:
  - Edamame 1 cup (17 g) or hummus with whole grain pita + hemp seeds sprinkled (3 tbsp hemp ≈ 10 g if needed)  
  - Totals: 17–27 g (cum ~137–147 g)

- Dinner:
  - Lentil and seitan stir-fry: 100 g seitan (25 g) or lentil stew 1 cup (18 g). If already near protein target, moderate portion to reach ~150 g.  
  - Totals adjust to hit ~150 g

Notes:
- A practical approach is 1–2 scoops protein powder and one dense serving (tempeh/seitan) plus legumes and soy milk across the day.
- If seitan is used, be aware it’s wheat gluten (avoid if gluten-sensitive).

Daily macro split example (for ~2000–2400 kcal target — adjust individually)
- Protein: 150 g = 600 kcal (25–30% calories)
- Fat: 60–80 g = 540–720 kcal (25–35% calories) — include nuts, seeds, oils
- Carbohydrate: remainder (approx 220–300 g) for energy and recovery

Supplement recommendations (consider with client and doctor)
- Vegan protein powder (pea, soy isolate, or blend) — convenient to hit protein targets.
- Creatine monohydrate — 3–5 g/day (evidence-supported for strength and mass gains).
- Vitamin B12 — essential for vegans (cyanocobalamin or methylcobalamin as directed).
- Vitamin D (if deficient or during winter) — check levels and supplement accordingly.
- Omega-3 (algal DHA/EPA) — optional for cardiovascular/neurological support.
- A daily multivitamin/mineral if diet may lack micronutrients.

Practical meal strategies and tips
- Pre-plan and batch-cook high-protein items: tempeh, seitan, lentil stews, marinated tofu.
- Use protein powders to boost shakes, oats, and baking.
- Add seeds (hemp, chia) & nut butters to smoothies and bowls.
- Rotate protein sources for amino acid variety and to prevent monotony.
- Prioritize post-workout meal within 1–2 hours with 25–40 g protein and carbs (e.g., smoothie + banana + oats + protein powder; or tempeh rice bowl).

Recovery and recovery programming
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours/night.
- Active recovery: light mobility, foam rolling, walking on rest days.
- Hydration: aim for at least 2–3 L water/day (more with sweat).
- Track progress: body weight, photos every 2 weeks, lift performance weekly.
- Massage/soft-tissue work as needed.

Monitoring and adjustments
- If weight doesn’t increase after 2 weeks, increase daily calories by 200–300 kcal (preferably from carbs and healthy fats).
- If strength stalls or excessive fatigue appears, re-evaluate sleep, stress, caloric intake and consider an extra deload week.
- Protein target: if 150 g is consistently hard, increase use of protein powders and seitan/tempeh; ensure each meal has a clear protein component.

Example week (mid-phase sample week — Week 6) summarised
- Mon: Upper A (as per Day 1 Week 5 template)
- Tue: Lower A (as per Day 2)
- Wed: Rest (light mobility)
- Thu: Upper B
- Fri: Lower B
- Sat: rest / optional light cardio
- Sun: Rest

Safety notes
- Squat and deadlift technique should be coached to prevent injuries. Use conservative loads for new PR attempts and always warm up adequately.
- If client has any medical conditions or allergies, consult their physician before starting supplements or large dietary changes.

If you want, I can:
- Customize the program more precisely to the client’s bodyweight, current 1RM numbers or exercise preferences.
- Provide a printable 12-week calendar with exact loading progressions (e.g., %1RM weekly targets).
- Create a 7‑day meal plan with recipes and grocery list hitting 150 g protein/day and specified calorie target — tell me estimated calorie needs or bodyweight and activity level.
